answer: Stop sybils with a river of trust that can only flow through a reef of mutual attestations. Each identity stakes a bond and earns standing only when trust flows to it through independent paths; a farm's clones all drink from the same few sponsors, so the min-cut between the farm and the honest graph is thin, and rewards through that cut are throttled to a trickle no matter how many names the farm mints. Every epoch a gale of random audits sweeps the graph: any identity whose attestors fail together loses its bond and the bonds of its sponsors, so N clones risk roughly N squared in slashing.
